content: WikiDoc provides a reference manager that enables users to insert references using their PubMed ID numbers. When you move the text, the reference automatically moves with it. All references are inserted at the bottom of the article, and clicking on a reference takes you directly to the cited article. This system is designed to be simple and efficient. In traditional referencing methods, you would typically type a number in the text, such as (1) or 1, to indicate a citation, and then manually add the reference details at the end of the article. However, WikiDoc discourages this approach in favor of its automated reference manager. The advantages of the WikiDoc reference manager include automatic numbering of references, the ability for references to move with the text, and clickable references that lead directly to the source article. Instead of manually typing references at the end of the article, the WikiDoc reference manager allows you to insert a code for the reference immediately after the material you wish to cite. This is done using a software program that generates the necessary code. The process for using the reference manager is as follows: 1. Use PubMed to locate the article you wish to cite. 2. Copy the PubMed ID (PMID) number, which is typically found at the bottom of the article's abstract. You can use the search function in your browser to locate the term PMID and its associated number. 3. Paste the PMID into a software program that generates Wiki language code for the reference. Examples of such software include: SUMSearch Biomedical Citation Maker DOI Wikipedia reference generator DTU Informatics PMID to Cite journal OttoBib for ISBNs Dave's Template Filler for various IDs (e.g., DrugBank, HGNC, PubMed, PubChem, URLs) 4. Ensure the add ref tag option is selected in the software. 5. Submit the information to generate the Wiki language code. 6. Copy the generated Wiki language code. 7. Paste the code into your article where you want the superscript reference number to appear. For example, if you are citing a study by Gibson et al., the generated code might look like this: ``` {{cite journal | author = Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, et al. | title = Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 | journal = Am. Heart J. | url = }} ``` This code would produce a superscript reference number in the text, linking to the full citation at the bottom of the article. If you prefer not to use the reference manager, you can manually type references. To do this, insert `<ref>` tags immediately after the sentence where you want the footnote number to appear. Between the `<ref>` tags, type the text of the note. If you plan to use the same reference multiple times, assign a unique name to the reference to avoid duplication. To make references appear at the bottom of the article, use the following code: ``` <references /> ``` This will generate a reference list in small font, formatted in two columns, with links to the original articles and abstracts. The output will look something like this: ↑ J Fam Pract. 2000 Oct;49(10):921-3.
